facts.raw_span: an 8-month history of radicular pain radiating from her lower back down the left leg
occasional tingling
denied any weakness, autonomic symptoms, history of trauma, or injury
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
normal muscle strength, normal abduction and adduction
negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography showed neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
most severe at L5, with no denervation
a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
measuring approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and demonstrated peripheral rim enhancement
causing severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs
MR neurography confirmed that the mass arose from the sciatic nerve at the left ischial groove

concepts.why: The presence of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone, along with neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots, suggests a neurofibroma.
The characteristics of the cystic mass, including its location and imaging features, are consistent with a schwannoma.
The description of the cystic mass, including its size and location, is consistent with a Tarlov cyst.
The patient's symptoms, including radicular pain and hypesthesia, could be consistent with a lumbar disc herniation.
The patient's symptoms, including radicular pain and neuropathic irritation, are consistent with lumbosacral radiculopathy.
The presence of a cystic mass along the course of the sciatic nerve with severe foraminal stenosis and neuropathic irritation of the nerve roots without denervation is consistent with perineurioma.

rationales.F07: Neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots suggests a nerve-related condition.
rationales.F09: A solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone is highly suggestive of a nerve sheath tumor.
rationales.F11: The mass's appearance on MRI, with peripheral rim enhancement, is consistent with a nerve sheath tumor.
